answer:
**Segmentation models answer different interface and latency needs.** Mask R-CNN first localizes candidate objects and predicts masks for those regions. YOLO-style segmentation emphasizes efficient detection and mask prediction in a single-stage family. SAM is designed for promptable segmentation, so a deployment also needs a way to supply prompts or generate and select masks automatically. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.02643) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.12872)

For an industrial part, a large clean mask may be easy while a one-pixel crack is decisive. Evaluate tiny-defect recall, boundary accuracy, separation of touching instances, and stability under lighting changes. Family names alone do not determine speed: input resolution, implementation, hardware, and prompt-generation overhead can dominate.

**Pixels are not millimeters.** A mask's area or width becomes a physical measurement only with calibrated geometry. If the object lies on a known plane, a calibrated mapping can convert image coordinates. If depth varies, perspective and distance must be accounted for; the same pixel width can represent different physical sizes.

Measure end-to-end error in physical units on reference objects, including segmentation and calibration uncertainty. Occlusion, lens distortion, and reflections can bias measurements even when masks look plausible. Choose the smallest system that meets both quality and latency requirements, and allow uncertain cases to be rejected rather than displaying unsupported precision.

**Technical details and references.**

Mask R-CNN uses region proposals and per-region mask prediction, offering strong instance localization with proposal overhead. YOLO-style segmentation emphasizes fast single-stage detection/masks. SAM is promptable segmentation with broad transfer, but still needs prompts or an automatic mask proposal/selection pipeline and may be costly at required resolution. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.02643) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.12872)

For industrial use, compare end-to-end latency, tiny-defect recall, instance separation, mask-boundary accuracy, and robustness to lighting/material changes on the target hardware. Model-family names do not establish a universal speed ranking.

Pixel masks alone do not yield physical size. Calibrate optics and scale, correct perspective, and use depth or a known measurement plane. Evaluate measurement error in physical units and reject uncertain/occluded parts rather than reporting precise-looking dimensions from unreliable masks.
